I have been farming these 163 mu for 5 years now. After middle school I came back to the village, took over the family land, and rented more mu from relatives and neighbors who went to work in cities. My household has 4 people, and some of us work off-farm when the fields are not busy, so we have cash to buy inputs. Last year I planted wheat-maize on 100 mu, cotton on 30 mu, watermelon on 15 mu, broccoli on 10 mu, chili on 5 mu, and stevia on 3 mu. The yields were okay and I didn't lose money, so this year I will keep the same layout. I don't change what didn't fail.

The wheat is already in the ground from last fall. I use improved seed, and I will put 18 kg of nitrogen per mu — I apply compound fertilizer as base and then topdress urea at jointing. Phosphorus 6 kg per mu, potassium 4 kg per mu. I will irrigate 4 times: winter irrigation if it is dry, then at jointing, heading, and grain filling. I spray pesticide 3 times. I rotary till before planting wheat. Last year I got about 550 kg per mu, and I expect about the same this year.

For summer maize on the same 100 mu, I plant hybrid seed right after wheat harvest. I do no-tillage direct seeding because there is no time to waste — if I am 3 days late, yield drops. I will apply 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 4 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once at seeding if it is dry, once at big trumpet stage. Summer rain usually helps. Pesticide twice. I expect 600 kg per mu.

Cotton on 30 mu — I plough deep in spring. Hybrid seed. I will apply 13 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium per mu. Cotton needs potassium for the bolls. I irrigate 3 times and spray pesticide 4 times because bollworms always come. Expected yield 260 kg seed cotton per mu.

Watermelon on 15 mu — I plough deep. Hybrid seed. Watermelon needs water but you have to stop before harvest. I will irrigate 5 times, spray pesticide 3 times. I apply 10 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, 9 kg potassium per mu. The input dealer told me more potassium makes them sweeter, and last year my watermelons sold well. Expected yield 3000 kg per mu.

Broccoli on 10 mu — hybrid seed, rotary tillage. 12 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 7 kg potassium per mu. 5 irrigations, 4 pesticide applications. Expected 900 kg per mu.

Chili on 5 mu — improved seed, rotary tillage. 10 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium per mu. 4 irrigations, 4 pesticide applications. Expected 1600 kg per mu.

Stevia on 3 mu — improved seed, rotary tillage. This is a contract crop, a company buys the dried leaves. I apply 8 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, 5 kg potassium per mu. 3 irrigations, 2 pesticide applications. Expected 250 kg dried leaves per mu.

I know fertilizer is expensive this year, but I would rather apply a bit too much than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster — I have to pay back the money I borrowed for seeds and fertilizer. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. My neighbor Lao Wang has a similar sized farm and he applies about the same amounts. If I cut back and my yield drops, I lose money and face. So I stick with what worked last year and adjust only a little.
